title: Principal Component Analysis (PCA)
hook: Find the directions your data varies most, then keep only the top few - you compress many correlated features into a handful while retaining most of the signal.
key_points: Computes principal components: orthogonal directions of maximum variance in the data.
Projecting onto the top k components reduces dimensionality while preserving as much variance as possible.
Requires centering (and usually scaling) the data first.
Explained variance ratio tells you how much information each component carries.
Works best when features are correlated; uncorrelated features have nothing to compress.
content_html: Principal Component Analysis finds the axes of greatest spread in a dataset and lets you describe each data point using only the most informative of those axes. When many of your original features move together, PCA can capture nearly all of the variation with far fewer numbers.
extra_html:
How it works

After centering the data (subtracting the mean), PCA computes a covariance matrix and finds its eigenvectors - the principal components. The first component points in the direction of greatest variance, the second in the direction of greatest remaining variance orthogonal to the first, and so on. Keeping the top k components and discarding the rest gives a low-dimensional representation that minimizes reconstruction error. In practice this is done efficiently with singular value decomposition (SVD).

Why it matters

PCA is a fundamental preprocessing tool for removing redundant features, speeding up downstream models, and visualizing high-dimensional data by plotting the first two or three components. It also underpins many other techniques in signal processing and machine learning. The Wikipedia article covers the linear algebra in detail and is a solid reference for the different computational approaches.

related.title: k-Means Clustering
related.hook: Pick k cluster centers, assign every point to the nearest one, move each center to the mean of its points, repeat - clusters emerge without any labels.

related.hook: t-SNE and UMAP squeeze thousands of dimensions into two so you can see whether your model's internal representations form meaningful clusters.

flashcards.prompt: When does PCA have little to compress?

choices.text: When the data has been centered

flashcards.explanation_html: PCA works best when features are correlated; uncorrelated features have nothing to compress.

flashcards.prompt: What preprocessing step does PCA require before computing components?

choices.text: Adding random noise to each feature

flashcards.explanation_html: PCA requires centering (and usually scaling) the data first, then computes the covariance matrix and its eigenvectors.
